scope: 56-frame contact-window MiniMax-H3 flow-inversion probe at sigma 0.12
summary: The first protected flow-inversion probe decoded and preserved pixels outside the safety envelope, but sigma 0.12 increased robot-ROI temporal jerk by 10.01% and was rejected before full-video expansion.
evidence: The 56-frame result decoded completely and outside-safety exactness passed before encoding.
Mean robot-ROI jerk increased from 6.3177944 to 6.9500016, a ratio of 1.1000677.
Visual review also found the default delivery encode softer than the accepted v78 input.
lessons: For an already accepted composite, high flow-inversion sigma can regenerate too much appearance and amplify temporal motion even when spatial protection is exact.
Contact-window gating must precede a costly full-timeline run.
limitations: This was a 56-frame contact-window probe using third-party MiniMax-H3 NF4 weights, not official BF16 weights.
next_actions: Reduce sigma to 0.08, blend model detail conservatively, and encode the validation result at high quality.
